subject: ClearPath pilot: request for hard-region serve and no-fallback for PHI workflows
messages:
From: ClearPath Health <ops@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Thu, 2 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot request: hard-region & no-fallback for PHI workflows

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed internally, we're preparing a small PHI pilot (20k calls/day at peak) and security wants the inference to remain in our designated US commercial region with no automatic fallback to other variants or regions.

Specific asks: 
- Hard region lock to us-east-1 (no cross-region routing).
- No automatic model fallback. The pilot must always resolve to the pinned model variant we test (v2.1-phi) unless we explicitly change it.
- Audit logs for every request (including model variant and routing decision) retained for 365 days.

We're aiming to start the pilot week of 2/21. Procurement attached the latest MSA redlines and a CSV with the pilot scope. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and any schedule or cost implications?

Appreciate your help—this is high priority for our security board signoff.

—Alex (ClearPath ops)

Attachments: clearpath_msa_redlines.pdf, pilot_scope.csv
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearPath Health <ops@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: hard-region & no-fallback for PHI workflows

Folks—looping infra, product, and security/legal. ClearPath is requesting a hard-region lock to us-east-1, no-fallback to any other model/region, and 365-day audit retention for a PHI pilot starting ~2/21. They attached redlines + pilot scope.

Ask: can we support a temporary (pilot-length) exception to our default fallback and routing policies, and what are the operational/cost tradeoffs? If we can't do a straight no-fallback, propose the least risky alternative we can offer that meets their compliance needs.

Marcus — can you outline infra options (dedicated pool, pinned variant, private deployment) and whether audit logging retention is feasible in hosted?
Irene — what additional contractual language or controls do we need to accept a no-fallback clause for PHI data?
Grace — product implications (rollout, monitoring, fallback safety nets) and whether Optimize/Console supports the visibility they want.

I'll consolidate; target quick internal decision by EOD 2/3 so we can reply to procurement.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of GTM Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearPath Health <ops@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Feb 2028 14:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: hard-region & no-fallback for PHI workflows

Short answer: feasible for a pilot with constraints. Details below.

Options (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted, pinned variant + region hardlock (least dev effort):
   - We can pin their route to model v2.1-phi and enforce region routing to us-east-1 via smart routing rules.
   - We must disable automatic cross-region fallback for their tenant (requires a routing-exemption flag).
   - Cost: will reduce our ability to route to cheaper/available pools; we should convert to dedicated burst capacity to guarantee latency. Estimated incremental monthly cost for pilot ~ $18k–$30k depending on peak concurrency.

2) Dedicated reserved pool (medium effort):
   - Provision a small dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 for the pilot. Guarantees isolation and no fallback.
   - Ops impact: provisioning lead time 7–10 days; infra to configure autoscaling policies and audit hooks. Cost higher but predictable.

3) Private deployment (highest effort):
   - On-prem or VPC private install — meets strictest compliance but requires customer infra & longer lead time. Not realistic for a three-week pilot.

Audit logs retention: we can capture request-level routing decisions and model variant in our observability pipeline and mount a 365-day retention window. We'll need to ensure logs include encrypted request IDs and are exported to a retention bucket (cost estimate included).

Implementation caveats:
- We must add a routing-exemption flag on their tenant to honor no-fallback; this bypasses some of our circuit-breaker fallbacks (risk: higher error exposure during infra incidents).
- For safety, recommend a canary timeout policy that fails cleanly (503) rather than transparently falling back to another model.

If you want, we can spin up a dedicated pool in us-east-1 for the pilot and set the tenant to pinned-mode with audit export. Need signoff from Security/Legal on accepting the operational risk.

Marcus
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearPath Health <ops@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 08:51:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: hard-region & no-fallback for PHI workflows

Thanks — high-level OK with an exception for a limited pilot, subject to conditions below:

Required controls before we can approve: 
- Tenant routing-exemption flag must be timeboxed (pilot start/end dates) and reversible via control plane without code deploy.
- KMS integration: customer keys OR dedicated KMS for pilot; all logs and backups must be encrypted with a customer-managed key or an RBAC-controlled Redwood key with strict access logs.
- Audit schema: include timestamp, request-id, model_variant, route_decision, serving_node_id, and operator-initiated changes. Must be exportable to a customer S3 bucket via a signed role.
- Operational SLA carveouts documented: we will not accept transparent fallback; instead we will return explict error codes on unavailable capacity. This must be reflected in the contract redlines.

Legal requested alterations to the MSA redlines (see attachment) to cover the temporary exception and to limit our liability during the pilot. Procurement should sign an addendum that lists the scope and pilot dates.

If infra proceeds with a dedicated pool, security will run a quick configuration review (24–48 hours) before enabling the exemption.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: ClearPath Health <ops@clearpathhealth.com>, procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Feb 2028 15:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: hard-region & no-fallback for PHI workflows

Alex / ClearPath team—thanks for the clear ask and materials. Summary of what we can offer for the 3-week pilot starting 2028-02-21: 

1) Implementation: provision a small dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 and enable a timeboxed routing-exemption flag that pins all requests to v2.1-phi. Exemption window: 2028-02-21 through 2028-03-13.
2) No automatic fallback: the tenant will return a documented error (503/NO_CAPACITY) if capacity is unavailable rather than falling back to another model/region.
3) Audit & retention: request-level logs (including model_variant and route_decision) exported to a signed S3 location for 365 days. Logs encrypted with a Redwood-managed key; customer-managed KMS supported if requested (please confirm).
4) Cost & timeline: recommended path is dedicated pool — provisioning lead time 7–10 business days; estimated pilot incremental cost $20k/month (final quote from finance attached to follow).
5) Contract: Irene requested a timeboxed addendum to the MSA limiting liability during the pilot and documenting the operational behavior. Please review attached redlines; we can deliver a DocuSign packet by EOD 2/6 once procurement confirms.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm KMS preference (customer-managed or Redwood) and sign addendum by 2/6.
- Procurement@clearpathhealth.com: confirm budget approval and preferred billing entity.
- Marcus & Ops: I'll schedule the provisioning work and security review (INF-1289).

If we get confirmation by 2/6 we'll be on track for a 2/21 pilot start.

Thanks everyone — will keep the thread updated with the Jira ticket and DocuSign link.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of GTM Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
